Quiet Table, third pass

This board has three parts. Part A is the record of what you approved, with each of your changes applied. Part B draws again the two screens you sent back: the city screen and diplomacy. Part C is new: the faith screen, the answer to "anything we're missing?", and four screens that were not drawn before.

Tags: approved is settled and shown with your change. proposed needs your word. Comment by id, for example "frame-b2-a".

The "today" pictures are from the current build (19 November), a bot game at turn 101. The mock-ups are HTML over screenshots. Paintings marked "stand-in" are wonder paintings in a slot that has no art yet. The typefaces are the game's own six faces from Google Fonts; a system stack takes their place if they are blocked. Card texts and figures are samples.

proposedThe Declare war button: two versions

The button must look important and must be hard to press by accident. Both versions use a dark red that is not the cinnabar of the next step, a blade mark, and a place at the bottom left, far from Propose. I recommend A. It is the more forceful of the two, it tells the player what follows before the act, and the game has a confirm card already. B is faster, but a player must learn it, and it is harder for a keyboard.

B1The city screen, quiet level, with levies and faith

Your four comments: keep the build queue as it is, keep the wonders segment, add a separate segment for empire buildings, and draw levying and the faith panel into the screen. The frame is drawn at 1280 px so that the town's hexes keep their room.

What changedThe left panel holds what the town does: growth (with the levy button), borders, citizens and faith. A band at the foot of the map holds what stands in the town: buildings, great houses, wonders here. I moved those three out of the left panel because one panel with all seven segments is about 920 px tall, and no window has that height. The build queue on the right is today's queue: no pictures, the same rows and prices. The levy menu opens beside the button, over the map. The faith segment shows the rite the town keeps and the rites it could start.
Splash art slotOnly the wonders segment: a 16:9 thumbnail, 60 by 34 px. The build queue has no picture.

Cost to build or to draw: Medium to large. The band takes about 160 px of the map's foot between the two panels. At 1180 by 700 the left panel is still tight, so the faith segment must close to one line there and open on a click. This frame is still a start; the final layout needs its own board.

The game's name for an empire building is a "great house" (the In play screen and the rules use it). Fourteen buildings are one to a realm today: the Forum, the Caravanserai, the Bourse, Chart the Stars, The Turning Heavens, The Alchemical Codex, the Mouseion, the Bimaristan, the Tophane, the Heroic Epic, the Imperial Throne, the High Temple, The Valley of Kings and The Magnum Opus. The rules mark which of them count as great houses; the segment should read that mark, not a list. A great house has the small seal, because In play counts it as a thing you hold.

B2Diplomacy: two layouts

Your comment: five columns are busy, the leader selector should be somewhere else, the portrait should be the main focus, and the leader's words should be more prominent. The ribbon version is dropped. Both layouts below have no courts column and no standing column.

What changedLayout A reads from the top: who is here (a row of faces), the portrait with the leader's words beside it in the display face, then one paper with two halves. The two trays of today become the "Add" chips inside each half, so the working part is two columns. Layout B makes the portrait larger, puts the words on a slip over its foot, and keeps today's two trays as two columns, with the table as one line under them.
Splash art slotLeader portrait, 3:4: 228 by 304 px in A, 330 by 440 px in B, and a 28 px circle in the row of faces. Count: one for each of the 13 leaders. Fallback: the seat's charge on its colour.

Cost to build or to draw: Medium for either. A changes how a deal is built (chips inside the paper), so it needs care with the deal rules. B keeps today's trays and is the smaller change.

I recommend A. The words are the largest text on the sheet, which is what you asked for, and the eye has one path: face, words, paper, button. B gives the portrait more room, but the words become a caption and the right side is still three blocks.

What the leaders say today

The game has twelve spoken lines, and every leader says the same ones. They are below, with the moment for each. No leader has a line of their own, a greeting, or a line for a first meeting. So "more speaking" needs writing: about four to six lines for each of 13 leaders (a greeting, a yes, a no, a threat, a line for war and one for peace). That is a job to schedule, and it belongs with the leader design pass.

WhenThe line
The paper is empty, in peace“Let us put something useful on the table.”
The paper is empty, at war“You have my attention. Speak.”
The answer is on its way“One moment. Let me consider it.”
An exchange is signed“A fair exchange. My merchants will see it done.”
Peace is agreed“Let the fighting end. We have an agreement.”
An exchange is refused“These terms do not suit us. What else can you offer?”
Peace is refused“Not yet. I am not ready to end this war.”
You ask for their last copy“I will not part with our last incense. Ask for something we can spare.”

C1The faith screen

The Faith sheet has three tabs today: Rites, Bonuses, and Religion & followers. The frame keeps the three tabs and their words. It changes the head and the Bonuses tab, and gives the Rites tab the light touch.

What changedThe head is the religion: its name as the title, with the holy city and the count of towns that follow. A realm with no religion keeps the title "Faith". The two large boxes at the top of Bonuses become one fine line. The gods, the beliefs and the holy city are tablets, the form they have on the In play screen: an arched top, a round vignette, the name in the card face, the pay figure at the foot. An empty place is a dashed tablet. The Rites tab is a plain table.
Splash art slotBelief vignette, 1:1, shown as a circle of 62 px. Count: one for each belief and god (the old plan said 18; the pantheon wheel shows more places). Fallback: the belief mark as an engraved seal.

Cost to build or to draw: Medium. The tablet exists on In play, so the form is not new. The third tab (the pantheon wheel, who follows, the clergy) keeps its layout and takes the kit only. One level only: a richer level would put the tablets on cloth, and your rule for offers says paper.

The four drawn below, and why these four:

  • The Order draft offer (C3). It is the most frequent choice in the game, and it still shows plain panels while the Council shows engraved cards. It should be one card in both places.
  • The Reliquary (C4). The great person card you approved needs its home, or the offer and the collection would show two different cards.
  • Game setup, the leader step (C5). It is the first place a player meets a leader, and it is the largest leader slot.
  • The unit panel and combat forecast (C6). It is the panel a player sees most, and its teal buttons are the one colour in the game that belongs to neither look.

Left for later: the deal notice and the war dispatch (they wait for your diplomacy layout), and the Compendium (the kit covers it, and a wonder entry gets the window).

C6The unit panel and the combat forecast

Both are working parts on the map, so both are plain. This frame removes a colour, it does not add a look.

What changedThe teal action buttons become the plain button of the kit, with the key at the right. Disband is apart, as a rubric link, because it cannot be taken back. The five boxed figures become one grid of mono figures with two meters. The forecast is a small ledger: each side's strength lines, a total, and the health after the blow. A line that a card pays has the small seal.
Splash art slotNone. A unit has no painting.

Cost to build or to draw: Small. I drew the forecast from its rules (flat strength lines on one ledger) and did not capture it; check it against the real one before a build.

Removed since the second pass: the painting in a toast, in the build queue and in the star chart. A painted thing has its own screen.

The rules of the style, updated

  1. Paper is the working interface. Panels, sheets, lists, tables, tooltips and buttons are flat parchment with ink text and mono figures. This includes the build queue, the unit panel and the forecast.
  2. Engraving marks what you hold: an Order, a Doctrine, a government, a wonder, a great house, a belief, a great person, a legacy. In a list or a toast, a held thing has only the small seal (a ring and a dot).
  3. A technology, a resource, a building and a unit are never engraved.
  4. Lapis and gilt mark a moment. The ribbon stands behind a wonder and an age, over the board. The full lapis page is for the ending only. No ribbon on a working sheet.
  5. Gilt is a hairline, never a fill, outside a card. Every sheet head has the same rule: ink over gilt.
  6. A painting appears only in the window, and only on a screen made for it: a plate, an offer, the Reliquary, diplomacy, setup, the faith tablets, the title, the ending. Never in a toast, a queue, a table or a tooltip.
  7. Every window has a fallback of the same size.
  8. The dark cloth is the card table (the Council, In play, the star chart). An offer opens on paper.
  9. Colour has a job. Cinnabar is the next step, at the bottom right. Dark red with the blade is war, at the bottom left, and it asks first. No other button has a fill.
  10. These never change: the ink top bar, End turn, the × to close, today's tab words, plain words, the town banners.

Questions for you

  1. Diplomacy: layout A or layout B? (B2.) And may I schedule the writing of each leader's own lines with the leader design pass?
  2. Declare war: A (a solid button, then a sheet that asks) or B (press and hold)? (A11.)
  3. The city screen: is the band at the foot right for buildings, great houses and wonders, with growth, levies and faith on the left? Or do you want all of it in the left panel, with segments that open and close? (B1.)
  4. Are the four new frames right as drawn: the Order draft (C3), the Reliquary (C4), setup (C5) and the unit panel (C6)? And is the loss ending (A9) approved with the win?
